- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70 → 75+), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% downward buffer to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33), model tends to lag behind true price drops; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged true values.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model overconfidently assumes mean reversion; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 10d high.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility clustering; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 10–20%.
